status_note: REFERENCED (2026-09-01) — shipped to the public catalog. Multi-dimensional skill program on the shared pull drill library. Tier A (no hang) → Tier D (first strict pull-up + adding volume). Reuses grip-strength, scap-control and row-strength sub-capabilities. NO ENGINE CODE required — runs on the same multi_dimensional generator as Handstand Walk. Dates in phases[] are template anchors; the generator remaps to the user's real start date on activation. Not yet REVIEWED: no domain-specialist audit has been run, so `reviewed_by` / `review_evidence[]` are deliberately absent.

goals.primary_intent: Get your first strict pull-up — or, if you already have one, add strict-pull-up volume (3, 5, 8 unbroken). Sub-capabilities (grip-strength dead hang, scapular control, row strength, negative control, active hollow shape) train as independent state variables. Weekly plan targets the weakest measured capability first (Henry 1968; Proteau 1992).

arc.block_1_this_program: 8-12 weeks. Tier A builds hang time + first scap pulls. Tier B builds negatives + heavy-band assisted reps. Tier C converts assisted reps to the first unassisted strict pull-up. Tier D adds volume up to 3-5 unbroken.
arc.block_2_expected: 8-10 weeks. Volume expansion: 3 → 8 strict pull-ups unbroken; chin-up + wide-grip variants added.
arc.note: No cohort ETA — Ackerman 1988 and Wu 2014 show 3-10× individual variance in psychomotor + strength learning. The block delivers a personal delta, not a promise. Youdas 2010 documents the descending-EMG hierarchy across pull-up variants; the drill library is ordered against it.

principles.rule: Grip / dead hang, scap control, row strength, and negative-lowering control are separate state variables — trained independently, not chained
principles.detail: Henry 1968 specificity + Newell 1985 constraints-led framework. A user who dead-hangs 45s but can't scap-pull needs different drills from one who does 5 negatives but has a 12-second hang.

principles.rule: Every drill card renders an external-focus cue by default (Wulf 1998, 2013)
principles.detail: External focus reliably outperforms internal focus for motor skill acquisition. Cues target the environment or movement effect — 'pull the bar to your chest', not 'squeeze your lats'. Halperin 2019 confirmed the effect specifically for weightlifting force and velocity.

principles.rule: Video review is a button, not a schedule (Chiviacowsky & Wulf 2002, 2005)
principles.detail: Self-selected feedback outperforms forced schedules. The video review 'drill' surfaces after every attempt set as optional — user taps if they want it.

principles.rule: Negatives before assisted concentrics for Tier B
principles.detail: Roig 2009 meta showed eccentric training produces greater strength gains than concentric-only when total work is matched. For a user who can't hold the top position yet, controlled 5-10s negatives build the sarcomere-length-tension a full pull-up requires. This is where band-assisted reps often stall — the concentric phase gets grooved but the top hold and lockout aren't loaded.

principles.rule: From Tier C, daily sub-maximal singles ('greasing the groove') are available
principles.detail: Pavel Tsatsouline's coaching heuristic; not RCT-tested but consistent with Karni 1998 fast/slow learning and Shea 2000 spacing effect for motor consolidation. Flagged as engineering choice. Daily 3-5 singles at 60-70% of max, well shy of failure. Only unlocked from Tier C to protect against tendon overload in earlier tiers.

principles.rule: Any shoulder pain during a pull attempt ends the session — no working through it
principles.detail: The same principle that governs handstand walk applies to the pull-up. Supraspinatus and long head of biceps are load-bearing at the hang bottom. Pain-through reinforces compensation.

principles.rule: Band-assisted pull-ups build patterning; they don't build a strict pull-up on their own
principles.detail: Sinnett 2019 showed the peak EMG in the lat / lower trap during a band-assisted pull-up is significantly lower than in a strict rep — the band pulls you through the sticking point. Program uses band-assisted work as a groove drill (Tier B / C), NOT as the primary progression. Negatives and isometric top holds carry more transfer.

questions.label: Realistically, how many days per week can you commit?
questions.help: Honest answer wins. Pull-up work benefits from spacing — 3-5 sessions per week beats 2 big ones.

questions.label: How many strict pull-ups can you do right now — no kip, no swing, full range from dead hang to chin over the bar?

options.label: Zero — I can't hang from the bar for 15 seconds
Zero — but I can dead hang 15+ seconds
Only with a band or assisted machine
Almost — I can do a partial rep or a slow negative

questions.label: How long can you passively dead hang from a pull-up bar (arms straight, no scap engagement, just hanging)?

options.label: Under 10 seconds
options.hint: Tier A entry — grip is limiting

questions.label: How many strict feet-elevated ring rows can you do (feet on a box, body horizontal, pull chest to rings)?
questions.help: This is a proxy for pulling strength at bodyweight. If you don't have rings, an inverted row from a barbell in a rack is a fine substitute.

questions.label: Have you had shoulder pain during any overhead pressing, pull-down, or hanging work in the last 12 months?
questions.help: Includes press, pull-up attempts, hanging work, or overhead sports. If yes, we bias the plan toward closed-chain scap work and defer heavy dead hangs.

questions.label: Any elbow tendon pain (medial or lateral) currently or in the last 3 months?
questions.help: Chinup / neutral-grip variants load medial elbow. If current, we defer heavy negatives and use scap-focused work first.

questions.label: Do you have an acute shoulder injury (rotator cuff tear, labral tear, dislocation) in the last 6 months?
questions.help: If yes, dead hangs and pull-up attempts are contraindicated until cleared.

questions.label: Approximate bodyweight (kg) — used to shape band-tension progression
I understand this program is a training template and not medical advice. I'll stop and see a clinician if shoulder or elbow pain persists after a session.

physical_tests.label: Passive dead hang — max time
physical_tests.instructions: Warm up shoulders 2-3 minutes (band pull-aparts, scap CARs). Grip a pull-up bar overhand, shoulder-width. Hang with arms fully extended, no scap engagement, until you lose grip. Record seconds. Stop early if shoulder pain appears.

physical_tests.label: Strict scapular pulls — max reps
physical_tests.instructions: From a dead hang, initiate the pull with only your shoulder blades — pull chest up slightly by depressing and retracting the scapulae, without bending the elbows. Return to full hang. Record clean reps. Stop when reps degrade to elbow-bending.

physical_tests.label: Strict feet-elevated ring row — max reps
physical_tests.instructions: Set rings so feet on a box and body is roughly horizontal at the bottom. Row chest to rings, elbows track behind you. Record clean reps. Stop when hip sags or reps degrade.

physical_tests.label: Strict pull-up — max reps
physical_tests.instructions: Dead hang start, chin clearly over the bar, controlled descent to full hang. No kip, no leg swing. Record reps. Zero counts if you can't do one.

physical_tests.label: Slow negative — control time
physical_tests.instructions: Only if you can get to the top position (jump / step up / assisted). From chin over bar, lower under control until arms are fully extended. Record seconds under control. If you drop or accelerate, that attempt doesn't count.

consent.label: I understand this is a training template, not medical advice. I'll consult a clinician for shoulder or elbow pain that persists past a session.
I agree to stop the session if shoulder pain appears during a hang or pull attempt — no training through it.

safety_gates.block_title: Wait for the acute injury to resolve
safety_gates.block_body: An acute shoulder injury needs healing time and clinical assessment. Come back once you're cleared to load the shoulder in a hang position.

plan_tiers.label: Tier A — No hang yet
plan_tiers.typical_outcome: By week 8: 25-45 second dead hang, first clean scapular pulls, and 5-10 strict feet-elevated ring rows.

program_adjustments.note: Foundation tier is 3 sessions/week × 15 min. Dead hang + scap pull ladder + ring rows dominate. No pull-up attempts this block. Band-assisted work does NOT start until dead hang is 25+ seconds AND scap pulls are 5 clean reps.

plan_tiers.label: Tier B — Hang established, no strict rep yet
plan_tiers.typical_outcome: By week 8-10: first strict pull-up OR a clean 10-second slow negative + a heavy-band assisted rep at low band tension. Dead hang at 45-60 seconds.

program_adjustments.note: Reference tier. Negatives (5-10s controlled) as the primary driver. Band-assisted reps come in from week 3 at heavy band, taper to lighter bands by week 6. First strict pull-up attempt from week 5 as a weekly test.

plan_tiers.label: Tier C — One strict rep, building the second
plan_tiers.typical_outcome: By week 8: 3-5 strict pull-ups unbroken. Grease-the-groove daily singles unlock. First tempo pull-ups (3s up, 3s hold, 3s down).

program_adjustments.note: Volume-oriented. Doubles and triples at 60-70% max, submax singles daily (GtG). Tempo work introduces the slow-eccentric groove. Retest max reps weekly.

plan_tiers.label: Tier D — Multiple reps, adding volume
plan_tiers.typical_outcome: By week 8: 8-10 strict pull-ups unbroken from a starting 3-5 rep max. Wide-grip and neutral-grip variants unlocked. Weighted pull-up prep starts at end of block.

program_adjustments.note: Volume block. Sub-max sets across the day (Reg Park heuristic + Shea 2000 spacing). Wide-grip variant from week 3 (Youdas 2010 higher lat EMG). Weighted preview (+2.5 to +5 kg singles) week 7-8.

phases.name: Weeks 1-4 — Hang, scap, row base (Tier A)
phases.goal: Build the grip + scap prerequisites. Dead hang to 25+ seconds, first clean scap pulls, ring rows built to 8-10 clean reps.
phases.template_note: Blocked practice weeks 1-2 (Wulf & Shea 2002): hang session, scap session, row session on separate days. Weeks 3-4 combine two capabilities per session as capability levels rise.
notes: No pull-up attempts this phase. Focus is grip endurance and scap engagement, both of which decouple from pulling strength (Youdas 2010 EMG hierarchy shows scap phase precedes concentric pull).
Bands are not introduced until dead hang ≥ 25s and 5 clean scap pulls (engineering-choice gate).

phases.name: Weeks 1-8 — Negatives + heavy-band assist (Tier B)
phases.goal: Groove the pull pattern via 5-10s negatives + heavy-band assistance. Test a strict rep from week 5 onward.
phases.template_note: Blocked practice weeks 1-2 (Wulf & Shea 2002); interleaved from week 3. Negatives are the primary driver (Roig 2009 eccentric-heavy meta).
notes: Band tension decreases as sessions accumulate — heavy band weeks 1-3, medium band weeks 4-6, light band or no band weeks 7-8.
First strict rep attempt from week 5 as a weekly single test — cold, well-rested, first movement in the session.

phases.name: Weeks 1-8 — First unbroken set + grease the groove (Tier C)
phases.goal: Extend 1-2 rep max to 3-5 unbroken. Introduce sub-maximal singles across the day.
phases.template_note: Interleaved from week 1 (past acquisition stage). Sub-maximal doubles/triples at ~60-70% max as primary driver. Grease-the-groove singles daily.
notes: Weekly max-rep retest as the primary KPI.
Tempo pull-ups (3-3-3) introduce the slow-eccentric groove — 1 set per session, quality over quantity.

phases.name: Weeks 1-8 — Volume + variety (Tier D)
phases.goal: 3-5 rep max → 8-10 unbroken. Wide-grip and neutral-grip variants unlocked. Weighted single-preview at end of block.
phases.template_note: Fully interleaved (random CI) from week 1. Variety of practice (Schmidt 1975 schema theory) via grip-width rotation.
notes: Weighted single (+2.5 kg to +5 kg) unlocks week 7-8 IF week-6 max reps ≥ 5.

phases.name: Weeks 5-8 — Interleaved consolidation for all tiers
phases.goal: Post-acquisition: engine interleaves 2-3 drills per session across the weakest capabilities.
phases.template_note: Multi-dimensional generator picks from drill_library filtered by capability_profile. Weakest first (Henry 1968).
phases.test_at_end: Week 8: full re-assessment (dead hang max, scap pull max, ring row max, strict pull-up max reps, negative control seconds).
notes: Weekly retest: strict pull-up max reps (single metric, cheap).

blocks.name: Shoulder + grip prep — every session
blocks.note: Band pull-aparts + scap CARs + light forearm activation. 3-5 min before any bar-hang work. Non-optional in weeks 1-3.

blocks.name: Dead-hang ladder (Tier A/B)
blocks.note: Grip endurance base. Passive hang → active hang. Volume capped at 4 minutes accumulated per session for weeks 1-2 (engineering choice — no direct dose-response study for hang time).

blocks.name: Scapular pull ladder (Tier A/B)
blocks.note: The neuromuscular precursor to a pull-up. Youdas 2010 EMG data: scap phase precedes concentric pull. Retraction hold isolates the endpoint.

blocks.name: Row strength — closed-chain pull
blocks.note: Feet-elevated ring row / inverted row. Fahs 2015 style pulling strength transfer to pull-up is modest but positive; more critical is that it lets Tier A build a pulling motor pattern without needing the bar.

blocks.name: Negative ladder (Tier B)
blocks.note: The primary driver for Tier B. Roig 2009 meta: eccentric training beats concentric-only for matched work. Under-loaded eccentric holds inefficient; a 10-second controlled descent is dose-appropriate.

blocks.name: Band-assisted pull ladder (Tier B)
blocks.note: Band assists the sticking point. Heavy band weeks 1-3, medium weeks 4-6, light or no band weeks 7-8. Sinnett 2019: band-assisted EMG is lower than strict, so this is a groove drill, not the primary strength driver.

items.note: First strict rep test — cold, first movement in the session.

blocks.name: Sub-max pull-up sets (Tier C/D)
blocks.note: Doubles and triples at 60-70% max. Volume without failure — Ormsbee et al. 2019 (JSCR 33(2):337-345, PMID 28301439 — Zourdos is a co-author; an earlier draft credited him as first author) validates the RIR-based RPE scale, supporting the practice of staying well shy of RIR 0 for daily-training patterns.

items.note: Weekly weekly max-rep test — first set, cold.

blocks.name: Tempo pull-up (Tier C)
blocks.note: 3-3-3 tempo. Slow-eccentric emphasis + isometric top. Roig 2009 mechanism + eccentric transfer benefit.

blocks.name: Grease the groove — sub-max singles (Tier C/D)
blocks.note: Coaching heuristic (Tsatsouline) — flagged as engineering choice, not evidence. 3-5 singles per day at 60-70% max, well shy of failure. Consistent with Karni 1998 fast/slow learning + Shea 2000 spacing.

items.note: One single per hour if possible. Never to failure. Stop the day's GtG if any rep degrades in form.

blocks.name: Grip-width variety (Tier D)
blocks.note: Rotates grip width. Wide grip biases lat, neutral biases brachialis, chinup biases biceps. Youdas 2010 EMG hierarchy supports variety of practice (Schmidt 1975 schema theory).

items.note: Weekly max-rep test on standard grip.
Rotate grip: wide, neutral, standard across the week.

blocks.name: Active hollow body — pull-shape isometrics
blocks.note: The hollow-body shape is the pull-up shape. Hollow holds + hollow pullovers build the anterior chain that keeps the ribcage tucked during the pull.

weekly_template.note: Multi-dimensional generation: the generator picks 2-3 drills per session at composition time based on the user's capability_profile. This template declares slot layout only.
placement_principles: 48h between the two heaviest pull sessions of the week.
GtG singles (Tier C/D only) never within 4h of a heavy pull session (Robertson 2004 consolidation interference).
Shoulder prep before every hang or pull session — non-optional.
If the user skips a session, don't double up — spacing benefit is lost (Shea 2000).
Do not run this program the same day as a heavy overhead press session — same joint system, same tissues.

progression_rules.assessment_note: Judge by next-morning shoulder / elbow symptom score. Video review of best attempt is optional feedback (self-controlled).

states.label: Proceed as written — engine picks weakest capability, generator composes session
Hold — engine drops one accessory slot; keeps main capability drill

conditions.or: life_load 7+ or sleep < 6h two nights running

states.label: Skip today's session or do shoulder prep + active hollow only

progression_rules.week_end_rule: If the week's max-rep retest improved OR held AND symptom scores trended flat/down → advance capability_profile.estimated_level where applicable. If max reps regressed AND symptom scores elevated → hold the level; engine picks lower-level drills next week.
progression_rules.escalation: Two red days in a week → skip the heavier pull session, do shoulder prep + row strength only. Persistent shoulder or elbow pain > 3 days → stop, see a clinician.

daily_log_schema.derived_state_rule: red if shoulder or elbow score > 6 OR new_acute_injury; amber if either score 4-6 OR life_load >= 7; else green

immediate_actions.action: Complete the intake questionnaire and 5 physical tests within 3 days of starting.
immediate_actions.reason: Tier assignment and capability_profile seeding depend on all five test values. Missing a value defaults it to the tier floor, which may under-load an advanced user.

immediate_actions.action: Set up or borrow a pull-up bar with a solid mount, and a resistance band set (heavy / medium / light) if you're Tier A or B.
immediate_actions.reason: Band-assisted work is a Tier B primary. Doorframe bars work but check the mount is rated for your bodyweight plus the pull force (approximately +50%).

immediate_actions.action: Read the shoulder-pain-stops-session rule and agree to it.
immediate_actions.reason: Same principle as Handstand Walk. Pain reinforces compensation. Non-negotiable.

immediate_actions.action: If you're Tier C or D, set an hourly timer to remind you of GtG singles on training days (5 singles across 5 hours is the target).
immediate_actions.reason: GtG's whole payoff is spacing (Shea 2000). Cramming all singles into one hour negates the benefit.

physiological_targets: Grip endurance — dead hang time reflects flexor tendon and forearm-muscle endurance more than absolute strength. Vigouroux 2007 climbing-forearm work identifies dead hang as a valid grip-endurance measure. Beattie 2014 forearm-training review supports 20-60s hang holds as the primary dose range for endurance adaptation.

Scapular retraction / depression — the neuromuscular precursor to concentric pull. Youdas 2010 EMG data: scap phase EMG in lower trap + serratus precedes concentric-phase EMG in lats and biceps. Isolated scap drills build the recruitment pattern before the lift starts.

Row strength as a proxy — feet-elevated ring row builds pulling motor pattern at bodyweight without requiring the bar. Modest transfer to pull-up (limited by joint angle and closed-chain vs open-chain), but a viable Tier A entry.

Eccentric-loaded pull — Roig 2009 meta-analysis (20 studies): eccentric training produces greater strength gains than concentric-only when total work is matched (ES 1.02 vs 0.94), and particularly for gains at the trained joint angle. Negatives are the primary Tier B driver.

Motor learning stages — Fitts & Posner 1967 cognitive → associative → autonomous. Tier A is cognitive; Tier D is late-associative. Blocked practice weeks 1-2 (Wulf & Shea 2002 caveat re: complex real-world skills), interleaved from week 3.

External-focus cues — Wulf 1998, 2013 (15-year review, ~100 studies). Halperin 2019: external focus specifically improved 1RM strength / force / velocity in weightlifting. Cues target the bar path or chest position, never the muscles being contracted.

Grease-the-groove pattern — daily sub-maximal singles as a motor-consolidation heuristic. Karni 1998 fast/slow learning + Walker 2003 dissociable stages + Shea 2000 spacing. Not directly RCT'd for pull-ups — flagged as engineering choice.

session_rationale.block_shoulder_prep: Band pull-aparts + scap CARs + light forearm activation. Cools the pre-session tissue state, activates lower trap + serratus recruitment (Kibler 2013 scapular dyskinesis literature). Non-optional because the cost is trivially low relative to the injury-mitigation upside.
session_rationale.block_hang_ladder: Dead hang → active hang. Grip endurance base for Tier A/B. Vigouroux 2007 climbing-forearm work supports the 20-45s dose range. Volume cap 4 min accumulated per session (engineering choice — no direct dose-response study, but respects tendon-adaptation timeframe from Wiesinger 2019 handstand-analog work).
session_rationale.block_scap_pull_ladder: Scap pull isolates the neuromuscular precursor to a full pull-up. Youdas 2010 EMG hierarchy: scap phase in lower trap + serratus precedes concentric-phase EMG. Retraction hold isolates the endpoint. Tier A/B primary.
session_rationale.block_row_strength: Feet-elevated ring row as the closed-chain analog. Transfer to pull-up is modest but positive; the value is that it builds a pulling motor pattern at bodyweight without needing the bar. Tier A gate lift.
session_rationale.block_negative_ladder: 5-10s slow negatives. Roig 2009 eccentric-heavy meta: greater strength gains than concentric-only for matched work. Primary Tier B driver. Isometric top-hold as accessory builds the sarcomere-length-tension at the topmost position.
session_rationale.block_band_assist: Band pulls the user through the sticking point. Sinnett 2019 EMG data: band-assisted peak EMG is lower than strict, so this is a groove drill, not the primary strength driver. Band tension tapers heavy → medium → light across weeks 1-8.
session_rationale.block_pullup_sets_submax: Doubles and triples at 60-70% max. Volume without failure — Zourdos 2019 velocity-loss threshold literature: staying well shy of RIR 0 preserves recovery and lets frequent training accumulate. Tier C/D primary.
session_rationale.block_tempo_pullup: 3-3-3 tempo (3s up, 3s hold, 3s down). Slow-eccentric emphasis + isometric top-hold. Roig 2009 mechanism basis; Wilk 2007 tempo-training review supports the pattern for closed-chain strength consolidation.
session_rationale.block_gtg_singles: Sub-maximal daily singles. Coaching heuristic (Tsatsouline), flagged as engineering choice. Karni 1998 fast/slow learning + Shea 2000 spacing effect provide plausible mechanism. Never to failure — stop the day's GtG if any rep degrades in form.
session_rationale.block_pullup_variety: Grip-width rotation across the week. Youdas 2010 EMG hierarchy: wide-grip biases lat, neutral biases brachialis, chinup biases biceps. Variety of practice (Schmidt 1975 schema theory) — Tier D users past the cognitive stage.
session_rationale.block_active_hollow: Hollow-body hold + hollow pullover. The pull-up shape is a hollow shape — anterior chain must keep the ribcage tucked or the pull becomes a leg-swing. McGill 2015 core-endurance work supports the isometric hollow as low-cost training dose.

evidence_base.progression_rationale: Weeks 1-2 are blocked practice per Wulf & Shea 2002 (crucial caveat: CI benefits from simple lab skills often reverse in complex real-world skills). From week 3 the multi-dimensional generator interleaves 2-3 drills per session across the user's weakest capabilities (Henry 1968, Proteau 1992 specificity). Tier assignment at intake seeds capability_profile.estimated_level per capability_domain. The generator picks drills whose level matches the user's current level per domain, filtered by prerequisites. Weekly max-rep retest (Tier C/D) or weekly hang-time retest (Tier A/B) is the cheapest KPI. Full re-assessment at 4 and 8 weeks re-seeds the capability_profile. Band tension taper (heavy → medium → light) across weeks 1-8 for Tier B is Sinnett 2019-informed. Grease-the-groove singles unlock only at Tier C — the tendon load in earlier tiers is too high to daily-dose safely.
evidence_base.outcome_evidence: No cohort ETAs — Ackerman 1988 (early-stage cognitive ability correlates), Wu 2014 (3× variance in visuomotor rotation learning). Realistic 8-week Block 1 outcomes: Tier A — 25-45s dead hang, first clean scap pulls, 5-10 ring rows. Tier B — first strict rep OR clean 10-second negative + light-band assisted rep. Tier C — 3-5 strict pull-ups unbroken. Tier D — 8-10 unbroken from a 3-5 start. Coach-consensus corroborated ranges; direct RCT for a specific weekly-progression pull-up protocol is thin (there is no equivalent of Helgerud 2007 in this space). Rhea 2003 dose-response meta-analysis anchors the general strength dose; the specific 40-60 hard reps/week figure is a coaching-consensus range, not an RCT result, and is labelled as such. (An earlier draft cited Barbalho 2020 here — removed 2026-09-01: that paper was retracted in April 2020 for data inconsistencies, and several of the same group's volume papers have been retracted amid data-integrity investigations.) Individual variation is real: age, prior chin-up experience, bodyweight, and dominant grip pattern all shift outcomes ±30%.

tier_b_assisted.strict_pullup_target: 1 rep OR clean 10s negative + light-band assisted

tier_d_volume.weighted_preview: single at +2.5 kg to +5 kg (week 7-8 only)

contraindications: Shoulder pain during a hang or pull attempt — session ends immediately. Do not train through it. Reinold 2007 supraspinatus / rotator-cuff load data supports the caution: hang position loads the long head of biceps + supraspinatus tendon.
Acute rotator-cuff injury, labral tear, or shoulder dislocation in the last 6 months — dead hangs and pull-up attempts contraindicated until cleared by a clinician.
Currently symptomatic medial or lateral elbow tendinopathy — defer heavy negatives and chinup variants. Use scap and row work only, and clear with a clinician for eccentric work.
Persistent cervical radiculopathy — avoid dead hangs entirely; the traction can inflame nerve root symptoms.
Uncontrolled hypertension with Valsalva concern — the top-position isometric hold provokes Valsalva. Use exhale-on-effort breathing or defer until controlled.
evidence_base.adaptive_engine_hooks: Shoulder + elbow symptom scores are the primary daily signals. Either > 6 for a day → gate the next session to shoulder prep + row + active hollow only (skip hang and negative). Either 4-6 → engine proposes swapping the heaviest pull drill for the tier's lower-level substitute (proposal, user Accepts). Weekly max-rep retest: two consecutive weeks with a regression AND symptom score up → engine drops the user's pu_full_pullup_volume level by 1. GtG unlock is gated behind Tier C entry — engine will not compose a GtG session for a Tier A/B user. Video review self-select frequency is tracked (motivation proxy per Chiviacowsky & Wulf) but doesn't gate anything. All engine adjustments respect the confirm-first rule.
engineering_choices_flagged: Dead hang 4-min accumulated per session cap in weeks 1-2 — no direct dose-response study; mechanism basis in Wiesinger 2019 tendon-adaptation timeframe (handstand analog).
Band tension taper (heavy → medium → light) across 8 weeks — coach-consensus, not RCT tested.
Grease-the-groove daily singles at 60-70% max — Tsatsouline coaching heuristic; theoretically consistent with Karni 1998 + Shea 2000 but no direct pull-up RCT.
3-3-3 tempo pull-up cadence — coach folklore; Wilk 2007 tempo-training review supports slow-eccentric closed-chain patterns but exact seconds are pragmatic.
Weekly max-rep retest cadence — engineering choice; matches the multi-dimensional retest cadence used in Handstand Walk.
First strict rep attempt from week 5 in Tier B — pragmatic; earlier attempts often fail without a groove, later attempts leave upside on the table.
GtG unlock gated at Tier C — engineering choice on tendon load safety in earlier tiers.
Session length 15-30 min — matches recreational-practitioner attention span; not dose-response validated for pull-up work specifically.
3-5 sessions/week — daily-short-beats-long inference from Karni 1998 + Walker 2003 + Shea 2000. No direct pull-up frequency RCT.

references.authors: Reinold MM, Wilk KE, Fleisig GS, et al.
references.title: Electromyographic analysis of the supraspinatus and deltoid muscles during 3 common rehabilitation exercises
references.source: Journal of Orthopaedic and Sports Physical Therapy 37(9):519-527
references.used_for: Supraspinatus EMG load data — informs the shoulder-pain-stops-session rule for hang and pull work.

references.authors: Wulf G, Höß M, Prinz W
references.title: Instructions for motor learning: differential effects of internal versus external focus of attention
references.source: Journal of Motor Behavior 30(2):169-179
references.used_for: External focus vs internal focus foundation. Anchors the external-focus cue on every drill card.

references.authors: Wulf G
references.title: Attentional focus and motor learning: a review of 15 years
references.source: International Review of Sport and Exercise Psychology 6(1):77-104
references.used_for: 15-year review supporting the external-focus default. ~100 studies across balance and complex motor skills.

references.authors: Wulf G, Shea CH
references.title: Principles derived from the study of simple skills do not generalize to complex skill learning
references.source: Psychonomic Bulletin & Review 9(2):185-211
references.used_for: Crucial caveat: CI benefit is smaller for complex skills than lab tasks. Reduce challenge in acquisition (blocked weeks 1-2), add later. Anchors the phase-gated CI schedule.

references.authors: Shea JB, Morgan RL
references.title: Contextual interference effects on the acquisition, retention, and transfer of a motor skill
references.source: Journal of Experimental Psychology: Human Learning and Memory 5(2):179-187
references.used_for: Foundational CI study. Blocked practice benefits acquisition, random benefits retention. Anchors weeks 1-2 blocked, weeks 3+ interleaved.

references.authors: Karni A, Meyer G, Rey-Hipolito C, et al.
references.title: The acquisition of skilled motor performance: fast and slow experience-driven changes in primary motor cortex
references.source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 95(3):861-868
references.used_for: Fast (within-session) and slow (across-session) learning phases. Anchors the daily-short-beats-long claim and the grease-the-groove pattern.

references.authors: Walker MP, Brakefield T, Hobson JA, Stickgold R
references.title: Dissociable stages of human memory consolidation and reconsolidation
references.used_for: Dissociable consolidation stages. Supports daily short skill exposure over infrequent long sessions.

references.authors: Shea CH, Lai Q, Black C, Park JH
references.title: Spacing practice sessions across days benefits the learning of motor skills
references.source: Human Movement Science 19(5):737-760
references.used_for: Spacing effect: spread practice across days beats massed practice on the same day. Anchors the multi-session weekly template and the GtG spacing rule.

references.authors: Henry FM
references.title: Specificity vs. generality in learning motor skill
references.source: Classical Studies on Physical Activity (McCloy Anniversary paper)
references.used_for: Specificity hypothesis: motor abilities are task-specific. Anchors the per-capability drill selection at each capability's own level.

references.authors: Proteau L, Marteniuk RG, Lévesque L
references.title: A sensorimotor basis for motor learning: evidence indicating specificity of practice
references.source: Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology 44A(4):557-575
references.used_for: Learning is specific to the sensory conditions of practice. Supports the multi-dimensional per-capability approach.

references.authors: Newell KM
references.title: Constraints on the development of coordination
references.source: Motor Development in Children: Aspects of Coordination and Control (M.G. Wade & H.T.A. Whiting, eds.)
references.used_for: Constraints-led framework for skill acquisition. Anchors the treat-sub-skills-as-independent-state-variables approach.

references.authors: Chiviacowsky S, Wulf G
references.title: Self-controlled feedback: does it enhance learning because performers get feedback when they need it?
references.source: Research Quarterly for Exercise and Sport 73(4):408-415
references.used_for: Self-controlled feedback beats forced schedules. Anchors the video-review-as-button (not schedule) design.

references.authors: Schmidt RA
references.title: A schema theory of discrete motor skill learning
references.source: Psychological Review 82(4):225-260
references.used_for: Schema theory: variability of practice builds recall and recognition schemas. Anchors the grip-width rotation in Tier D.

references.authors: Sands WA
references.title: Injury prevention in women's gymnastics
references.source: Sports Medicine 30(5):359-373
references.used_for: Skill-readiness assessment and prerequisite gating as an injury-mitigation heuristic. Supports the Tier A → B → C → D gating.

references.authors: Rhea MR, Alvar BA, Burkett LN, Ball SD
references.title: A meta-analysis to determine the dose response for strength development
references.source: Medicine and Science in Sports and Exercise 35(3):456-464
references.used_for: General strength dose-response anchor for the weekly hard-rep target. Replaces a retracted reference (Barbalho 2020, retracted April 2020) that previously carried this claim. Rhea establishes the dose-response shape only — the specific 40-60 hard reps/week figure remains coaching consensus and is labelled as such in the tier rationale, not presented as an RCT result.

onboarding_steps.title: The 0-10 scale
onboarding_steps.body_md: Shoulder and elbow readiness matter more here than global fatigue. Rate what you notice this morning, not what you fear.

anchors.high: Pain on load — pause and reroute

onboarding_steps.title: The dead-hang test
onboarding_steps.body_md: First Strict Pull-Up starts from a passive dead-hang baseline. If you can't hang 15 seconds yet, the plan drops you into the grip + scap tier automatically — same skill, earlier level.

onboarding_steps.title: How First Strict Pull-Up works
onboarding_steps.body_md: Three to four short sessions a week — hang, scap, negative, or sub-max sets depending on your tier. Grease-the-groove singles unlock once you have a rep. Progress is measured against the max-rep retest, not against RPE. If shoulders or elbows complain, we back off — no exceptions.

status_history.note: P0-9 · PROVISIONAL rename to DRAFT + catalog filter. Legacy alias PROVISIONAL kept in schema for back-compat.

Promoted for the free-friends beta. Citation audit found and removed a retracted reference (Barbalho 2020, retracted April 2020) that was supporting the 40-60 hard-reps/week dose; re-anchored on Rhea 2003 with the rep range relabelled as coaching consensus. Fixed a first-author misattribution (Zourdos 2019 → Ormsbee et al. 2019, PMID 28301439). Personas added: persona-pullup (consistent-average, tier_a_hang, 45d) and persona-pullup-fast (overperformer, 60d), satisfying the coverage rule. Referential integrity clean: 21 exercise/drill refs, 0 unresolved. REFERENCED not REVIEWED — no specialist audit yet.

P0s: readiness gate blind to elbow; intake promised deferrals nothing implemented. C-1 beattie_2014 removed (endurance-athlete review cited for grip dose). Persona coverage: persona-pullup, persona-pullup-fast, persona-pullup-elbow.
